[[File:Complex fbsp wavelet.PNG|thumb|Frequency B-spline wavelets: cubic spline fbsp 3-1-2 complex wavelet.]]
In applied mathematics, '''fbsp wavelets''' are '''frequency [[Spline wavelet|B-spline wavelet]]s'''.

These frequency B-spline wavelets are complex wavelets whose spectrum are [[spline (mathematics)|spline]].

: <math> \operatorname{fbsp}^{(m-\mathrm{fb}-f_c) }(t) := {\sqrt {\mathrm{fb}}} \operatorname{sinc}^m \left( \frac {t} {\mathrm{fb}^m} \right) e^{j2 \pi f_c t}   </math>

where [[sinc function]] that appears in [[Shannon sampling theorem]].

* ''m'' > 1 is the order of the spline
* fb is a bandwidth parameter
* ''f<sub>c</sub>'' is the wavelet center frequency

The [[Shannon wavelet]] (sinc wavelet) is then clearly a special case of fbsp.

* O. Cho, M-J. Lai, A Class of Compactly Supported Orthonormal B-Spline Wavelets in: ''Splines and Wavelets'', Athens 2005, G Chen and M-J Lai Editors pp.&nbsp;123–151.
* M. Unser, Ten Good Reasons for Using Spline Wavelets, ''Proc. SPIE'', Vol.3169, Wavelets Applications in Signal and Image Processing, 1997, pp.&nbsp;422–431.
